note.ja: 閉殻RHFの占有空間軌道の式で、非局所交換を含む。既存のHe局所還元とH2のRHF例を保持する。追加は固定H2/H3+の最小2電子模型で、UHF式は別の対応模型に明示する。一般多中心分子、開殻の大域安定性、完全基底や一般相関法の保証ではない。
note.en: Closed-shell occupied-orbital RHF equations include nonlocal exchange. Preserve existing He local-reduction and H2RHF examples. New calculations cover only fixed minimal two-electron H2/H3+ models; UHF equations have their own mapped model. No general multicenter molecules, global open-shell stability, complete-basis or general correlated-method guarantee.

note.ja: 密度汎関数の局所KS代表形です。公開例は、球対称Heのスピン非偏極・Dirac交換のみLDAと、固定した周期He／He₂セルのLDA交換＋VWN5相関です。原子の動径実装と周期PySCFワークフローは別系列で、基底・境界条件・参照も異なります。各例の範囲は下の固定入力・検証記録で確認してください。GGA・hybrid・一般物質・励起状態まで検証した意味ではありません。
note.en: Representative local Kohn–Sham equations. Published examples cover spin-unpolarized exchange-only Dirac LDA for spherical helium and LDA exchange plus VWN5 correlation for fixed periodic He/He₂ cells. The radial atomic implementation and periodic PySCF workflows are separate series with different bases, boundaries and references. Inspect each input and validation record below; these examples do not validate GGA, hybrids, general materials or excited states.

note.en: Fixed-nuclei nonrelativistic electronic eigenproblems; add nuclear repulsion separately. Preserve the existing hydrogenic radial examples. name.en: Helium: closed-shell HF and exchange-only LDA

note.ja: 孤立・球対称・閉殻1s²に限定した原子単位の動径式。RHFのvH/2は2電子同一空間軌道に特有。LDAは交換のみで相関なし。UHF、GGA、hybrid、一般分子・周期DFTの実行例ではない。
note.en: Atomic-unit radial equations restricted to isolated spherical closed-shell 1s² helium. The RHF vH/2 form is specific to two electrons sharing one spatial orbital. LDA is exchange-only, without correlation; no UHF, GGA, hybrid, general molecular or periodic-DFT example.

scope.en: Compare spherical 1s² closed-shell helium HF and spin-unpolarized Dirac exchange-only LDA. No electron correlation, molecules or periodic systems.

assumptions.ja: 非相対論・無限質量の点核、2電子が単一1s空間軌道を二重占有。2次中心差分と線形密度混合。HF交換の局所還元はこの2電子問題に限定。
assumptions.en: Nonrelativistic infinite-mass point nucleus, two electrons doubly occupying a single 1s spatial orbital. Second-order central differences and linear density mixing. Local HF exchange reduction is specific to this two-electron problem.
